subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Intermediate and Advanced Transformations (W10 B2)

questions.stem:
Convert to passive voice:
'The committee approved the new policy last week.'

options.option_text: The new policy was approved by the committee last week.
The new policy has been approved by the committee last week.
The new policy is approved by the committee last week.
The new policy had been approved by the committee last week.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Simple past active → was/were + past participle passive. 'The committee approved' (simple past) → 'was approved by the committee'. The time phrase 'last week' is retained. Trap: 'has been approved' (present perfect) conflicts with 'last week'; 'is approved' is simple present passive; 'had been approved' is past perfect passive — both wrong tenses for the original simple past.

questions.stem:
Convert to passive voice:
'The chef is cooking a special dish for the guests.'

options.option_text: A special dish is being cooked by the chef for the guests.
A special dish was being cooked by the chef for the guests.
A special dish has been cooked by the chef for the guests.
A special dish is cooked by the chef for the guests.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Present continuous active (is + V-ing) → present continuous passive (is/are being + past participle). 'The chef is cooking' → 'is being cooked by the chef'. Trap: 'was being cooked' = past continuous passive (wrong tense); 'has been cooked' = present perfect passive; 'is cooked' = simple present passive — all wrong for continuous tense.

questions.stem:
Identify the correct passive form:
'Someone has stolen my wallet.'

options.option_text: My wallet is stolen by someone.
My wallet was stolen by someone.
My wallet has been stolen.
My wallet had been stolen by someone.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Present perfect active (has + V3) → present perfect passive (has/have been + V3). 'Has stolen' → 'has been stolen'. Note: when the agent is unknown/unimportant ('someone'), the 'by phrase' is dropped. Trap: 'was stolen' = simple past passive (wrong tense); 'had been stolen' = past perfect passive; 'is stolen' = simple present passive.

questions.stem:
Convert to active voice:
'The book was being read by Sita when the lights went out.'

options.option_text: Sita is reading the book when the lights went out.
Sita had read the book when the lights went out.
Sita was reading the book when the lights went out.
Sita read the book when the lights went out.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Past continuous passive (was being + V3) → past continuous active (was/were + V-ing). 'Was being read by Sita' → 'Sita was reading the book'. The context (ongoing action interrupted by 'lights went out') confirms past continuous. Trap: 'Sita read the book' (simple past) removes the continuous/ongoing aspect; 'had read' (past perfect) changes the tense entirely.

questions.stem:
Identify the passive transformation:
'They will announce the results tomorrow.'

options.option_text: The results will be announced tomorrow.
The results would be announced tomorrow.
The results are announced tomorrow.
The results shall have been announced tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Future simple active (will + V1) → future simple passive (will be + V3). 'Will announce' → 'will be announced'. Agent ('they') is omitted when general/unspecified. Trap: 'would be announced' is conditional (not future); 'are announced' is simple present passive; 'shall have been announced' is future perfect passive (wrong tense).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form of the modal sentence:
'The government should reduce taxes on essential goods.'

options.option_text: Taxes on essential goods should be reduced by the government.
Taxes on essential goods should have been reduced by the government.
Taxes on essential goods must be reduced by the government.
Taxes on essential goods are reduced by the government.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Modal + V1 passive = modal + be + V3. 'Should reduce' → 'should be reduced'. The modal 'should' is retained as-is. Trap: 'should have been reduced' is a perfect modal passive (implying it should have happened in the past but didn't — a different meaning); 'must be reduced' changes the modal (obligation vs recommendation); 'are reduced' drops the modal entirely.

questions.stem:
Identify the active voice of:
'Mistakes are often made in haste.'

options.option_text: People often make mistakes in haste.
One has often made mistakes in haste.
Mistakes were often made in haste.
Mistakes often make people in haste.

questions.explanation: A is correct. When there is no agent in the passive ('by phrase' absent), use 'one', 'they', or 'people' as the subject in the active. 'Are made' (simple present passive) → 'people often make' (simple present active). Trap: 'One has often made' shifts to present perfect (wrong tense); 'mistakes were made' stays passive; 'mistakes make people' reverses subject-object incorrectly.

questions.stem:
Transform to passive voice:
'Please submit your forms before Friday.'

options.option_text: You are requested to submit your forms before Friday.
Your forms are being submitted before Friday.
Submit your forms before Friday, it is requested.
Your forms must be submitted before Friday by you.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Imperative passive transformation: 'Please + V1' → 'You are requested to + V1'. The structure replaces the polite request with a formal passive ('you are requested to submit'). Alternative: 'It is requested that you submit…'. Trap: B uses present continuous passive (doesn't capture the imperative/request nature); D adds 'by you' (the 'you' as agent in imperatives is redundant and sounds awkward).

questions.stem:
Identify the passive form:
'The news surprised everyone at the meeting.'

options.option_text: Everyone at the meeting has been surprised by the news.
Everyone at the meeting was surprised by the news.
Everyone at the meeting is surprised by the news.
Everyone at the meeting had been surprised by the news.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Simple past active (surprised) → simple past passive (was/were + V3). 'The news surprised everyone' → 'everyone was surprised by the news'. Since 'everyone' = singular in grammar, use 'was' (not 'were'). Trap: 'has been surprised' = present perfect (wrong tense); 'is surprised' = present tense (wrong); 'had been surprised' = past perfect (changes meaning — implies surprise happened before another past event).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive transformation:
'No one could solve this problem.'

options.option_text: This problem could not be solved by anyone.
This problem cannot be solved by no one.
This problem was not solved by anyone.
This problem can not be solved by anyone.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Modal + not + V1 passive: 'Could not solve' → 'could not be solved'. 'No one' in active → 'by anyone' in passive (the negative is transferred to the auxiliary, not to the agent). Trap: B = double negative error ('cannot be solved by no one' has two negatives = positive — wrong); C = 'was not solved' drops the modal 'could'; D = 'can not be solved' changes 'could' (past) to 'can' (present).
